symptom: `mxcli playwright check /p/secret /p/items -p app.mpr --role User`, where User may not open /p/secret, printed `url=/login.html?messageCode=403#/secret  LOGIN PAGE` and `FAIL   the sign-in form is showing, not the page (pass --user/--password or --role)` for a user it had just signed in; every later run printed `login demo_user` again while the runtime's session count rose 1, 2, 3, 4, and /p/secret checked alone had its session signed out after every run
cause: LoginForm (#usernameInput present) was the whole sign-in test, and the client puts a refused page on the same form: the runtime answers POST /xas/ get_session_data (referrer /secret) with 403 and the client goes to /login.html?messageCode=403#/secret. NeedsLogin() read the refusal as a forgotten session, so the stale-session retry signed in beside the live session (a new one per run), and the no-page-past-the-form rule signed a valid session out
file: cmd/mxcli/docker/pagecheck_assert.go (AccessDenied, NeedsLogin, EvaluatePage), cmd/mxcli/docker/pagecheck.go (ACCESS DENIED in formatPageVerdict, wrongPage), cmd/mxcli/docker/pagecheck_check.go (credentials.roles/signedInAs; checkOrigin sets SignedInAs)
insight: Record the network before choosing a signal: a 30-line Playwright script logging navigations and /xas/ statuses settled it in one run per case. Signed in and refused: 403, then /login.html?messageCode=403#/<page>. Anonymous, and with a session the runtime forgot: 401, then /login.html#/<page>, guest access on as well (11.15) — the runtime checks authentication before page access, so a 403 never means a stale session. The DOM cannot tell them apart: login.js reads the code as messageCode.split('=')[1], which is undefined, so #loginMessage stays empty and hidden on both and its http403 text (translated anyway) never shows; title, heading and text=34 are identical. The one predicate drove all three symptoms — the wrong advice, the per-run session leak and the needless sign-out — because the retry and sign-out decisions hang on 'needs a login'; check what else reads a predicate before rewording only its message. Count sessions with M2EE runtime_statistics rather than trusting the verdict. Aside: without401 matched the chunk hash 85ce401445201 in the 11.15 client's [Startup] error, which is why 11.15 printed one FAIL line fewer than 11.13 — substring-matching '401' is luckier than it looks
